name: Kettle 2: Abandoned Carts
description: Shopify ops (project 9): every 30 minutes, a personal recovery email for each abandoned checkout, with an offer only when the rules allow one.

options.instructions:
You write a short, warm note from Hannah, who runs Kettle & Fern, a small online tea shop, to a customer who left tea in their cart.

- 60 to 100 words, plain text, two or three short paragraphs, starting with "Hi <first name>,".
- Mention what they picked by name and, for one item, a short tip taken from the shop's notes (brewing temperature, how to enjoy it). Use only the notes given; don't invent tasting notes or facts.
- If an offer is given, mention it once using its exact wording. If no offer is given, don't mention discounts, codes or free shipping at all.
- No pressure: no fake urgency, no "only a few left", no "last chance", no guilt.
- Don't include links, prices or a sign-off line; those are added for you. End with a friendly sentence.
- subject: under 50 characters, in sentence case (capital first letter), friendly, no shouting and no emojis. preheader: under 90 characters.

parameters.jsCode:
// One "contacted" write per email sent, so nobody is emailed twice.
return $('Compose').all().map(i => ({ json: { action: 'mark_contacted', checkout_id: i.json.checkout_id, offer: i.json.offer } }));

parameters.content:
## Kettle 2: Abandoned Carts
Every 30 minutes. **Pick Carts** (code) chooses who to email: not completed, has consent, not contacted yet, left 1-48 hours ago. It also decides the offer: the welcome code for first-time customers with $60 or more in the cart, a free-shipping nudge when they are within $15 of it, otherwise none.
**Write Email** (GPT-5.4 mini) writes a short personal note from the shop owner using the shop's product notes, and may only mention the offer it was given. **Compose** adds the items, offer box, button and footer. Each checkout is then marked so it is never emailed twice.
